raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Enable decode context parallelism (DCP) for Qwen4Exp QSA.

Each rank reads its own shard of the main KV cache. The QSA selector and its side caches stay replicated on every rank. The ranks then combine their partial results with the base-2 log-sum-exp convention that QSA uses.

Four further changes make this work:

- The selector and the main KV cache share one block table. In separate groups the selector takes most of the blocks that a request needs, and DCP loses capacity instead of gaining it.
- A packed compressed cache binds one whole manager block. Its kernel blocks are mapped afterwards through the stride between manager blocks. Without this the server stops at startup, because a packed block cannot be cut into evenly spaced kernel blocks.
- The QSA side caches skip their stores when the block table points at the null block.
- Every attention metadata builder in a group takes the block table row width that the runner allocated. A replicated layer in a DCP-sharded group has a larger block than the group, so a builder that derives the width from its own layer spec sizes its kernel block table too small. The mapping now rejects a row that does not fit instead of writing past it.

An empty DCP batch now returns both an output tensor and a log-sum-exp tensor.

Draft #61242 covers the same feature with a sharded selector. This PR keeps the selector replicated, so selection stays identical to DCP=1.

## Test commands

Focused suites:

```bash
pytest -q tests/v1/core/test_qsa_dcp_cache_policy.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_qsa_dcp_localize.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_qsa_selector_write_mask.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py
pytest -q tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py
```

Serving command. Set `--decode-context-parallel-size` to 1 or 2. Only the MTP runs pass `--speculative-config`:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 \
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 2 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 262144 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --enable-prompt-tokens-details \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

Load, AIPerf 0.12.0, started with `aiperf profile -f agentx.yaml`. In this scenario `concurrency: 128` is the number of multi-turn conversations that stay open at the same time. A conversation pauses between its turns, so it does not hold one request in flight at all times. The measured number of requests in flight is in the results table.

```yaml
      target: first_turn_prefix

    type: concurrency

```

GSM8K, EvalScope 1.12.0, three repeats with a fresh server each time. The generation config comes from the file in this repository:

```bash
  RUN="$run" python - <<'PYTHON'

    "no_timestamp": True, "limit": None,
})

assert s is not None and not s.incomplete
assert (s.requested, s.succeeded, s.errored, r.num) == (1319, 1319, 0, 1319)
print(f"GSM8K run {os.environ['RUN']}: {r.score:.4f}")
```

MRCR, one warmup and five scored repeats. The seed fixes the 24 samples, so every run scored the same items:

```bash
for run in 0 1 2 3 4 5; do
  python tests/evals/mrcr/mrcr_eval.py \
    --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \
    --num-samples 24 --needles 2 4 8 \
    --max-prompt-tokens 259840 --max-tokens 2048 \
    --seed 42 --concurrency 24 \
    --save-results "mrcr-run-$run.json"
done
```

## Unit test results

The suites in the commands above ran together on four B200 GPUs: 207 passed, no skips. Ruff check, Ruff format check, and `git diff --check` passed.

## Serving results

All four runs used four B200 GPUs in one node, with the same source commit and checkpoint. Each run used a fresh server and a prefix-cache reset. Every scored workload had zero request errors.

The table gives the mean and the peak number of requests in flight that each run measured. Output tokens per second per GPU divides the measured output rate by the four GPUs. Output tokens per second per user is the mean rate of one request stream.

| DCP | MTP | KV tokens | Requests/s | Completions | Requests in flight, mean / peak | Output tokens/s per GPU | Output tokens/s per user |
| ---: | :---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | off | 9,764,101 | 1.642852 | 1,495 | 58.4 / 95 | 343.3 | 31.7 |
| 2 | off | 17,585,863 | 2.330763 | 2,121 | 51.8 / 79 | 485.4 | 42.3 |
| 1 | on | 8,396,119 | 0.981313 | 893 | 53.1 / 69 | 185.7 | 25.2 |
| 2 | on | 14,565,287 | 2.142851 | 1,950 | 51.9 / 85 | 443.0 | 44.1 |

DCP=2 raised MTP-off throughput by 1.419x over DCP=1. No run reached 128 requests in flight, and the highest peak was 95. DCP=2 served more requests per second with fewer requests in flight, because each request finished sooner.

MTP drafted and accepted tokens at both DCP sizes. Mean acceptance length was 2.384924 at DCP=1 and 2.391250 at DCP=2, from counter deltas around each warmup and measured replay. With one MTP layer reused for three steps, MTP-on throughput was 0.597x of MTP-off at DCP=1 and 0.919x at DCP=2. On this long-context trace MTP costs throughput, and DCP returns most of that cost. At DCP=2, MTP raised the rate for one user from 42.3 to 44.1 output tokens per second while it lowered the rate for the whole node.

## Accuracy

GSM8K scored all 1,319 samples with zero errors in every run:

| Run | Three scores |
| --- | --- |
| DCP=1, MTP off | 0.9803, 0.9803, 0.9765 |
| DCP=2, MTP off | 0.9803, 0.9788, 0.9765 |
| DCP=2, MTP on | 0.9742, 0.9788, 0.9795 |

MRCR scored the same 24 samples with zero errors in each of five repeats:

| Run | Five scores in run order |
| --- | --- |
| DCP=1, MTP off | 0.863217, 0.868507, 0.898238, 0.898238, 0.863217 |
| DCP=2, MTP off | 0.863217, 0.895787, 0.898238, 0.901117, 0.895787 |
| DCP=2, MTP on | 0.898183, 0.868507, 0.898183, 0.898238, 0.898238 |

MRCR does not return one stable score on this model. Five repeats are too few to compare the runs. The individual scores are given because a mean hides this spread. The DCP=1 MTP-on run was measured for throughput only.

AI assistance was used. The submitter reviewed every changed line and the evidence.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

@sungsooha Hi, I opened a draft for the same feature, #61242. I found your PR only now (I missed it in the duplicate search, sorry). I will keep #61242 as a draft and not compete with this PR. Some data from our side in case it helps, and an offer.

**Different design point.** #61242 shards the QSA selector side caches too: each DCP rank scores only its own compressed blocks, takes a local top-k, and an exact stable global merge (all-gather of `[rows, k, 2]` candidates) gives the same top-k as DCP=1. Your PR keeps the selector and side caches replicated, which avoids that candidate all-gather. Ours saves more KV memory, but each QSA layer needs one more collective.

**A100 data** (8 × A100-SXM4-40GB, TP8 + EP, DCP=4, FP8 KV via the merged #60602, MTP 3, full MLPerf agentic set, 3 × 60 min, strict per-request SLO TTFT ≤ 2.93 s and TPOT ≤ 21.74 ms):
- GPU KV cache 2.18 M → 7.83 M tokens (3.6×). KV peak at concurrency 20 is 99 % → 29 %.
- The first version failed the SLO (82–88 % pass), because the sm_80 merge and localize glue launched 3.7× more kernels and made the step host-bound. One slow host then gated every collective (nsys).
- After Triton pack/merge, fused expand+localize reused across MTP passes, and a copy-free LSE combine with a fused gate, the pass rate was 95.1 / 96.1 / 96.6 %. Goodput was 2.07 req/s against 2.00 without DCP.
- A greedy 48-prompt check gives DCP=4 vs DCP=1 within the run-to-run noise of DCP=1.

**One thing to check when you rebase onto `main`:** since #60602, below sm_89 `forward_qsa` passes the FP8 cache as raw `uint8`, and the `2⁸` factor is folded into the host scales. The DCP reader must pass that through unchanged. The LSE must use the folded softmax scale. The combine itself needs no scale, because `v_scale·2⁸` acts only on the normalized partial outputs.

If useful, I can rebase our sm_80 pieces (Triton merge, MTP selection reuse, copy-free combine/gate) as a follow-up on top of yours, or share the A100 benchmarks and nsys analysis. How would you like to proceed?

@kimseunghyun-kr Thank you, and thank you for the A100 data. The host-bound finding and the fix list are the useful part.

I would like to keep this PR as the base. Please send the sm_80 pieces as a follow-up PR. The Triton merge, the MTP selection reuse, and the copy-free combine each stand on their own.

On your #60602 point: this branch is rebased past it. The kernel reads the e4m3 bytes as raw uint8 below sm_89, and the host folds the K dequant scale into softmax_scale. The V scale is folded per row. So the path reads correct, but I have only run B200. Your follow-up is where it gets tested on sm_80.

Your sharded selector is a real design point, not a lesser one. It saves more memory, and it avoids a packed-layout problem that our replicated selector hit at startup. An opt-in choice later would let a user trade memory against collectives.

Thanks, @sungsooha. Agreed: your PR stays the base. I will send the sm_80 pieces as a follow-up PR on top of `c9de36da9`.

First I am running an A100 A/B on 8 × A100-SXM4-40GB (DCP=4, FP8 KV, MTP 3, MLPerf agentic at 32 sessions): your branch as is, your branch plus our follow-ups, and our sharded-selector draft for reference. This also tests your FP8 path on sm_80. I will post the numbers here and link the follow-up PR.

@sungsooha While testing this branch on 8 × A100 for the follow-up, we found an engine start-up failure. It happens on `c9de36da9` with no other change.

### Summary

- **Problem:** at DCP 4 the engine fails at start (CUDA graph capture) with `unflatten: Provided sizes [140, -1] don't multiply up to the size of dim 1 (548)`. At some other shapes there is no error, but the selector's kernel block table is wrong.
- **Cause:** two places size the same block-table row with different block sizes. The runner uses the group block (480): 140 columns. `AttentionGroup.create_metadata_builders` uses the replicated selector's own block (480 × 4 = 1920): 137 columns. They round 137 blocks to different multiples.
- **Fix (how):** compute the row width once, from the group spec, with one helper (`get_kv_cache_group_block_table_width`). The runner uses it, and `init_attn_backend` passes the same number to `create_metadata_builders` (new optional `block_table_width`), so the kernel block table is always runner width × (layer block / kernel block). Here: 140 × 4 = 560.
- **Result so far (CPU, vLLM code of both branches imported as is, 3,564 shapes):** before the fix 1,276 shapes raise and 75 give a wrong table without an error; after the fix all 3,564 are correct, including the production shape and the short shape that was silently wrong. **GPU check is pending** (details at the end).

**Setup:** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, TP 8 + EP, DCP 4, `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1`, FP8 KV, `max_model_len` 262144, MTP 3, Model Runner V2, `--max-num-batched-tokens 2048`. The engine picks attention block 480. Prefix caching on or off gives the same result (reproduced twice).

**Error** (all workers, CUDA graph memory profile → `prepare_inputs_to_capture` → `build_attn_metadata` → `AttentionGroup.map_to_kernel_block_table`):
```
unflatten: Provided sizes [140, -1] don't multiply up to the size of dim 1 (548) in the input tensor
```

### Cause, step by step (line numbers at `c9de36da9`)

**1. The selector spec gets a block DCP times the group block.** [`qsa_cache.py#L871`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c9de36da9b9551908a0ded2fd3185ae2ebfafc63/vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/qsa_cache.py#L871) (from a4f387539):
```python
block_size = self.cache_config.block_size * dcp_world_size   # 480 * 4 = 1920
... dcp_sharded=dcp_world_size == 1,                          # False at DCP 4
```
This replicated 1920-token spec is placed in one uniform KV cache group with the DCP-sharded main KV (block 480). The group's kernel block size is 480, so each selector block is 4 kernel blocks.

**2. The runner sizes the group's block-table rows from the group spec.** [`model_runner.py#L640-L650`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c9de36da9b9551908a0ded2fd3185ae2ebfafc63/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L640-L650):
```python
max_num_blocks = spec.max_num_blocks_per_req(...)            # group spec, block 480, sharded
max_num_blocks = get_block_table_width(max_num_blocks, spec.block_size,
                                       token_alignment=spec.block_table_token_alignment)
```
- `max_num_blocks_per_req`: cdiv(262144, 480 × 4) = **137**
- [`get_block_table_width`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c9de36da9b9551908a0ded2fd3185ae2ebfafc63/vllm/v1/worker/block_table.py#L29-L41): block_alignment = 128 / gcd(128, **480**) = 4, so cdiv(137, 4) × 4 = **140** columns per row.

**3. The layer's metadata builder sizes its kernel block table from the layer (selector) spec.** [`worker/utils.py#L325-L340`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c9de36da9b9551908a0ded2fd3185ae2ebfafc63/vllm/v1/worker/utils.py#L325-L340) (this code is from main, #57169):
```python
max_num_blocks = self.kv_cache_spec.max_num_blocks_per_req(...)              # selector spec, block 1920, replicated
width = get_block_table_width(max_num_blocks, self.kv_cache_spec.block_size)  # alignment by block 1920
width *= self.kv_cache_spec.block_size // kernel_block_size                  # * 1920 // 480 = 4
self.kernel_block_table = torch.zeros(..., width, ...)
```
- `max_num_blocks_per_req`: cdiv(262144, 1920) = **137**
- block_alignment = 128 / gcd(128, **1920**) = 1, so the width stays **137**
- × 4 → **548** kernel columns.

**4. The crash.** [`worker/utils.py#L404-L409`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c9de36da9b9551908a0ded2fd3185ae2ebfafc63/vllm/v1/worker/utils.py#L404-L409) receives a group row of 140 columns:
```python
out = self.kernel_block_table[ubatch_idx, :rows, : cols * blocks_per_kv_block]   # [:, :, :560] -> only 548 exist
torch.add(..., out=out.unflatten(1, (cols, -1)))                                # 548 is not 140 * k -> error
```

**Why main is safe and this branch is not:** the code in step 3 assumes every layer spec in a group has the group's block size. On main that holds. Step 1 adds a layer with a larger block (and a different DCP sharding) to the group, so the two width formulas (steps 2 and 3) round 137 to different multiples.

**When it fails, and when it does not fail but is wrong.** I ran the exact formulas of steps 2–3 and the exact ops of step 4 on CPU (torch 2.10) over 21,888 shapes (group block 16–1024, DCP 2/3/4/8, `max_model_len` 1,024–300,000):

| Result | Shapes | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Widths agree | 15,596 | correct |
| Widths differ, kernel width not a multiple of the row width | 6,115 | `unflatten` raises (our crash) |
| Widths differ, kernel width **is** a multiple of the row width | **177** | **no error**: `unflatten` succeeds with an inner size < DCP, and `torch.add(..., out=...)` only warns "An output with one or more elements was resized … deprecated" and resizes the output. The returned kernel block table has the wrong width; row 0 holds only the first part of its blocks, and rows ≥ 1 hold wrong block ids. |

The silent cases are mostly short `max_model_len` with large blocks, for example block 480, DCP 4, `max_model_len` 1024: the runner row is 4 columns, the kernel table is 4 wide but needs 16, and no error is raised. Reproducer:

```python
import math, torch
cdiv = lambda a, b: -(-a // b)
width = lambda n, blk: cdiv(n, 128 // math.gcd(128, blk)) * (128 // math.gcd(128, blk))  # get_block_table_width
b, d, L = 480, 4, 1024
n = cdiv(L, b * d)
cols, W = width(n, b), width(n, b * d) * d          # runner row (step 2), kernel table width (step 3)
table = torch.full((1, 3, W), -7, dtype=torch.int32)
bt = torch.arange(3 * cols, dtype=torch.int32).view(3, cols)
out = table[0, :3, : cols * d]                       # worker/utils.py:404
torch.add(torch.arange(d, dtype=torch.int32), bt.unsqueeze(-1), alpha=d,
          out=out.unflatten(1, (cols, -1)))          # worker/utils.py:405-410: warns, does not raise
expected = (bt.unsqueeze(-1) * d + torch.arange(d)).reshape(3, cols * d)
print(cols, W, out.shape, expected.shape)            # 4 4 torch.Size([3, 4]) torch.Size([3, 16])
print([torch.equal(out[r], expected[r, :W].int()) for r in range(3)])   # [True, False, False]
```

The existing tests use `max_model_len` = 784 × 16 with 2-column block tables, so they reach neither case.

### Proposed fix

Commit [`8e212b229`](https://github.com/kimseunghyun-kr/vllm/commit/8e212b229) on top of `c9de36da9` (branch `kimseunghyun-kr:qsa-dcp-59279-blockfix`).

**Idea:** compute the row width in one place, from the group spec, and give that same number to the builders.

1. New helper `get_kv_cache_group_block_table_width(group_spec, vllm_config, max_len)` in `vllm/v1/worker/block_table.py`. It is the runner's formula from step 2, moved into one function. The V2 runner now calls it.
2. `init_attn_backend` calls the same helper for each group and passes the result to `create_metadata_builders`:
   ```python
   block_table_width = get_kv_cache_group_block_table_width(
       kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups[kv_cache_group_id].kv_cache_spec,
       vllm_config,
       vllm_config.model_config.max_model_len,
   )
   group.create_metadata_builders(..., kernel_block_size=kernel_block_size,
                                  block_table_width=block_table_width)
   ```
3. `create_metadata_builders` uses that width when it is given, and keeps the old per-layer formula when it is not:
   ```diff
   -   max_num_blocks = self.kv_cache_spec.max_num_blocks_per_req(...)
   -   width = get_block_table_width(max_num_blocks, self.kv_cache_spec.block_size)
   +   if block_table_width is None:
   +       max_num_blocks = self.kv_cache_spec.max_num_blocks_per_req(...)
   +       block_table_width = get_block_table_width(max_num_blocks, self.kv_cache_spec.block_size)
   +   width = block_table_width
       width *= self.kv_cache_spec.block_size // kernel_block_size
   ```

So the kernel block table is always "runner row width × blocks per kernel block". In our case: 140 × 4 = 560 columns.

Tests added in `test_qsa_dcp_cache_policy.py` (CPU): the production shape (group 140 vs selector spec 137), and a full-width row mapped at DCP 4.

Not changed: the V1 runner path. Encoder-decoder models (the runner widens their rows past `max_model_len`) behave as before.

### Does the fix work?

| | Correct | Raises | Wrong table, no error |
|---|---|---|---|
| `c9de36da9` (this PR) | 2,213 | 1,276 | 75 |
| `c9de36da9` + fix | **3,564** | **0** | **0** |

<details>
<summary>How this was checked (CPU, torch 2.10, 3,564 shapes)</summary>

For each shape (group block 16–1024, DCP 2/4/8, `max_model_len` 1,024–296,000), I imported each branch's vLLM code as is and called its own functions (no copied formulas):
1. `QSACompressedKeyCache.get_kv_cache_spec` (block × DCP) and a main `FullAttentionSpec`;
2. `get_kv_cache_groups`, and an `AttentionGroup` for the selector;
3. `create_metadata_builders`, with the same arguments `init_attn_backend` gives it in that branch;
4. the runner row width, with the same formula `model_runner.py` uses in that branch;
5. `map_to_kernel_block_table` on a full-width 3-row block table, compared value by value with the correct kernel table.

Not covered: the same path on GPU tensors, and a full engine start.
</details>

### Status

- ✅ CPU check above, ruff clean.
- ⏳ **GPU check pending:** the same 8 × A100 start at the same flags, with only this commit added. It waits for a free 8-GPU node; I will post the result here.

If useful, I can open this as a PR against your branch, or you can cherry-pick the commit.

detail.body:
## Purpose

Enable decode context parallelism (DCP) for Qwen4Exp QSA.

Each rank reads its own shard of the main KV cache. The QSA selector and its side caches stay replicated on every rank. The ranks then combine their partial results with the base-2 log-sum-exp convention that QSA uses.

Four further changes make this work:

- The selector and the main KV cache share one block table. In separate groups the selector takes most of the blocks that a request needs, and DCP loses capacity instead of gaining it.
- A packed compressed cache binds one whole manager block. Its kernel blocks are mapped afterwards through the stride between manager blocks. Without this the server stops at startup, because a packed block cannot be cut into evenly spaced kernel blocks.
- The QSA side caches skip their stores when the block table points at the null block.
- Every attention metadata builder in a group takes the block table row width that the runner allocated. A replicated layer in a DCP-sharded group has a larger block than the group, so a builder that derives the width from its own layer spec sizes its kernel block table too small. The mapping now rejects a row that does not fit instead of writing past it.

An empty DCP batch now returns both an output tensor and a log-sum-exp tensor.

Draft #61242 covers the same feature with a sharded selector. This PR keeps the selector replicated, so selection stays identical to DCP=1.

## Test commands

Focused suites:

```bash
pytest -q tests/v1/core/test_qsa_dcp_cache_policy.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_qsa_dcp_localize.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_qsa_selector_write_mask.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py
pytest -q tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py
```

Serving command. Set `--decode-context-parallel-size` to 1 or 2. Only the MTP runs pass `--speculative-config`:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 \
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 2 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 262144 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --enable-prompt-tokens-details \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

Load, AIPerf 0.12.0, started with `aiperf profile -f agentx.yaml`. In this scenario `concurrency: 128` is the number of multi-turn conversations that stay open at the same time. A conversation pauses between its turns, so it does not hold one request in flight at all times. The measured number of requests in flight is in the results table.

```bash
  RUN="$run" python - <<'PYTHON'
```

```bash

  python tests/evals/mrcr/mrcr_eval.py \

    --seed 42 --concurrency 24 \
    --save-results "mrcr-run-$run.json"
done
```

## Unit test results

The suites in the commands above ran together on four B200 GPUs: 207 passed, no skips. Ruff check, Ruff format check, and `git diff --check` passed.

## Serving results

All four runs used four B200 GPUs in one node, with the same source commit and checkpoint. Each run used a fresh server and a prefix-cache reset. Every scored workload had zero request errors.

The table gives the mean and the peak number of requests in flight that each run measured. Output tokens per second per GPU divides the measured output rate by the four GPUs. Output tokens per second per user is the mean rate of one request stream.

| DCP | MTP | KV tokens | Requests/s | Completions | Requests in flight, mean / peak | Output tokens/s per GPU | Output tokens/s per user |
| ---: | :---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | off | 9,764,101 | 1.642852 | 1,495 | 58.4 / 95 | 343.3 | 31.7 |
| 2 | off | 17,585,863 | 2.330763 | 2,121 | 51.8 / 79 | 485.4 | 42.3 |

| 2 | on | 14,565,287 | 2.142851 | 1,950 | 51.9 / 85 | 443.0 | 44.1 |

DCP=2 raised MTP-off throughput by 1.419x over DCP=1. No run reached 128 requests in flight, and the highest peak was 95. DCP=2 served more requests per second with fewer requests in flight, because each request finished sooner.

MTP drafted and accepted tokens at both DCP sizes. Mean acceptance length was 2.384924 at DCP=1 and 2.391250 at DCP=2, from counter deltas around each warmup and measured replay. With one MTP layer reused for three steps, MTP-on throughput was 0.597x of MTP-off at DCP=1 and 0.919x at DCP=2. On this long-context trace MTP costs throughput, and DCP returns most of that cost. At DCP=2, MTP raised the rate for one user from 42.3 to 44.1 output tokens per second while it lowered the rate for the whole node.

## Accuracy

GSM8K scored all 1,319 samples with zero errors in every run:

| Run | Three scores |
| --- | --- |
| DCP=1, MTP off | 0.9803, 0.9803, 0.9765 |
| DCP=2, MTP off | 0.9803, 0.9788, 0.9765 |
| DCP=2, MTP on | 0.9742, 0.9788, 0.9795 |

MRCR scored the same 24 samples with zero errors in each of five repeats:

| Run | Five scores in run order |
| --- | --- |
| DCP=1, MTP off | 0.863217, 0.868507, 0.898238, 0.898238, 0.863217 |
| DCP=2, MTP off | 0.863217, 0.895787, 0.898238, 0.901117, 0.895787 |
| DCP=2, MTP on | 0.898183, 0.868507, 0.898183, 0.898238, 0.898238 |

MRCR does not return one stable score on this model. Five repeats are too few to compare the runs. The individual scores are given because a mean hides this spread. The DCP=1 MTP-on run was measured for throughput only.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""QSA DCP selection localization and empty-owner behavior."""
+
+from importlib import import_module
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+PAD = -1
+
+
+def _owner(pos, world, interleave):
+    return (pos // interleave) % world
+
+
+def _local_id(pos, world, interleave):
+    return (pos // (world * interleave)) * interleave + (pos % interleave)
+
+
+def _reference_localize(row, world, rank, interleave):
+    """Plain enumeration. Returns (localized prefix, kept count)."""
+    kept = []
+    for g in row:
+        if g < 0:
+            continue
+        if _owner(g, world, interleave) != rank:
+            continue
+        kept.append(_local_id(g, world, interleave))
+    return kept, len(kept)
+
+
+def _pack(rows, width, device="cpu"):
+    """Build the packed buffer: selection columns plus a trailing count."""
+    out = torch.full((len(rows), width + 1), PAD, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    for i, row in enumerate(rows):
+        for j, g in enumerate(row[:width]):
+            out[i, j] = g
+        out[i, width] = len(row[:width])
+    return out
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="Triton kernel needs a GPU")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("world,interleave", [(2, 1), (2, 4), (4, 16)])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("width", [32, 2051])
+def test_kernel_matches_the_reference(world, interleave, width):
+    from vllm.models.qwen4_exp.nvidia.ops.qsa_dcp import qsa_localize_dcp_indices
+
+    rows = (
+        [list(range(0, 64, 2)), list(range(1, 40)), [], [7]]
+        if width == 32
+        else [list(range(width)), [0], []]
+    )
+    packed = _pack(rows, width).cuda()
+    source = packed.clone()
+    local = torch.empty_like(packed)
+    for rank in range(world):
+        expected = [
+            _reference_localize(row[:width], world, rank, interleave) for row in rows
+        ]
+        for _ in range(5 if width == 2051 else 1):
+            local.fill_(123)
+            qsa_localize_dcp_indices(packed, local, world, rank, interleave)
+            # The layer's selection buffer must survive: MTP steps read it again.
+            assert torch.equal(packed, source)
+            for row, (ids, count) in enumerate(expected):
+                assert int(local[row, width]) == count
+                assert local[row, :count].tolist() == ids
+                assert bool((local[row, count:width] == PAD).all())
+
+
+# --- contracts that keep the gate from being applied twice -------------------
+
+
+@pytest.mark.cpu_test
+def test_localize_leaves_the_source_alone_without_dcp():
+    """World size 1 still copies, so one call site covers both paths."""
+    from vllm.models.qwen4_exp.nvidia.ops.qsa_dcp import qsa_localize_dcp_indices
+
+    packed = _pack([[5, 6], [7]], 8)
+    source = packed.clone()
+    local = torch.empty_like(packed)
+    qsa_localize_dcp_indices(packed, local, 1, 0, 1)
+    assert torch.equal(packed, source)
+    assert torch.equal(local, source)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.cpu_test
+def test_the_kernel_wrapper_rejects_a_gate_with_return_lse():
+    """The output gate must be applied after DCP merging, not by the kernel."""
+    from vllm.models.qwen4_exp.nvidia.ops import qsa as qsa_ops
+
+    query = torch.zeros(2, 4, 64, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    cache = torch.zeros(1, 16, 2, 64, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    indices = _pack([[0], [0]], 8)
+    block_table = torch.zeros(1, 1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    token_to_req = torch.zeros(2, dtype=torch.int32)
+    args = (query, cache, cache, indices, block_table, token_to_req, False)
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="do not pass one"):
+        qsa_ops.qsa_sparse_paged_attention(
+            *args, output_gate=torch.zeros_like(query), return_lse=True
+        )
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="requires an output gate"):
+        qsa_ops.qsa_sparse_paged_attention(*args)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.cpu_test
+def test_empty_qsa_batch_returns_the_dcp_output_and_lse_pair():
+    """A rank with no query tokens still supplies both DCP merge inputs."""
+    from vllm.models.qwen4_exp.nvidia.ops.qsa import qsa_sparse_paged_attention
+
+    query = torch.empty((0, 4, 64), dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    cache = torch.empty((1, 16, 2, 64), dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    indices = torch.empty((0, 9), dtype=torch.int32)
+    block_table = torch.zeros((1, 1), dtype=torch.int32)
+    token_to_req = torch.empty((0,), dtype=torch.int32)
+
+    output, lse = qsa_sparse_paged_attention(
+        query,
+        cache,
+        cache,
+        indices,
+        block_table,
+        token_to_req,
+        False,
+        return_lse=True,
+    )
+
+    assert output.shape == query.shape
+    assert output.dtype == torch.float32
+    assert lse.shape == query.shape[:2]
+    assert lse.dtype == torch.float32
+    assert lse.device == query.device
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="QSA kernels need CUDA")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "world,interleave,seq_len,cache_dtype,k_scale,v_scale",
+    [
+        (2, 1, 64, torch.bfloat16, None, None),
+        (4, 16, 200, torch.bfloat16, None, None),
+        (2, 16, 64, torch.float8_e4m3fn, 0.75, 1.5),
+        (4, 4, 64, torch.float8_e4m3fn, 0.75, 1.5),
+        (2, 16, 64, torch.uint8, 0.75, 1.5),
+    ],
+)
+def test_sharded_ranks_reproduce_the_single_rank_result(
+    world, interleave, seq_len, cache_dtype, k_scale, v_scale
+):
+    from vllm.models.qwen4_exp.nvidia.ops.qsa import qsa_sparse_paged_attention
+    from vllm.models.qwen4_exp.nvidia.ops.qsa_dcp import qsa_localize_dcp_indices
+    from vllm.v1.attention.ops.dcp import _lse_weighted_combine
+
+    import_module("vllm.models.qwen4_exp.nvidia.model")
+    qsa_backend = import_module(
+        "vllm.models.qwen4_exp.nvidia.qsa"
+    ).Qwen4ExpQSAFlashAttentionBackend
+    assert qsa_backend.get_impl_cls().lse_base_on_e is False
+
+    torch.manual_seed(1234 + seq_len)
+    device = "cuda"
+    page = 16
+    num_kv_heads = 2
+    head_dim = 64
+    num_q_heads = 8
+
+    full_blocks = (seq_len + page - 1) // page
+    shape = (full_blocks, page, num_kv_heads, head_dim)
+    k_source = torch.randn(shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device)
+    v_source = torch.randn(shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device)
+    if cache_dtype in (torch.float8_e4m3fn, torch.uint8):
+        k_full = (k_source / k_scale).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+        v_full = (v_source / v_scale).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+        if cache_dtype == torch.uint8:
+            k_full = k_full.view(torch.uint8)
+            v_full = v_full.view(torch.uint8)
+    else:
+        k_full, v_full = k_source, v_source
+
+    local_len = seq_len // world + page
+    local_blocks = (local_len + page - 1) // page
+    local_shape = (local_blocks, page, num_kv_heads, head_dim)
+    k_rank = [
+        torch.zeros(local_shape, dtype=cache_dtype, device=device) for _ in range(world)
+    ]
+    v_rank = [
+        torch.zeros(local_shape, dtype=cache_dtype, device=device) for _ in range(world)
+    ]
+    for pos in range(seq_len):
+        rank = _owner(pos, world, interleave)
+        local_id = _local_id(pos, world, interleave)
+        k_rank[rank][local_id // page, local_id % page] = k_full[
+            pos // page, pos % page
+        ]
+        v_rank[rank][local_id // page, local_id % page] = v_full[
+            pos // page, pos % page
+        ]
+
+    num_rows = 6
+    selections = [
+        list(range(row, seq_len, row + 2))[: seq_len // 2] for row in range(num_rows)
+    ]
+    selections[0] = [0]
+    width = max(len(s) for s in selections)
+    global_sel = _pack(selections, width, device)
+
+    q = torch.randn(
+        (num_rows, num_q_heads, head_dim), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device
+    )
+    token_to_req = torch.zeros(num_rows, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    full_table = torch.arange(full_blocks, dtype=torch.int32, device=device).unsqueeze(
+        0
+    )
+    local_table = torch.arange(
+        local_blocks, dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+    ).unsqueeze(0)
+
+    reference, reference_lse = qsa_sparse_paged_attention(
+        q,
+        k_full,
+        v_full,
+        global_sel,
+        full_table,
+        token_to_req,
+        False,
+        k_scale=k_scale,
+        v_scale=v_scale,
+        return_lse=True,
+    )
+    assert reference.dtype == torch.float32
+    if cache_dtype == torch.uint8:
+        native_out, native_lse = qsa_sparse_paged_attention(
+            q,
+            k_full.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn),
+            v_full.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn),
+            global_sel,
+            full_table,
+            token_to_req,
+            False,
+            k_scale=k_scale,
+            v_scale=v_scale,
+            return_lse=True,
+        )

+        torch.testing.assert_close(reference_lse, native_lse, rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-3)
+
+    outs, lses = [], []
+    for rank in range(world):
+        local_sel = qsa_localize_dcp_indices(
+            global_sel, torch.empty_like(global_sel), world, rank, interleave
+        )
+        empty = local_sel[:, -1] <= 0
+        if rank:
+            assert bool(empty[0])
+        out, lse = qsa_sparse_paged_attention(
+            q,
+            k_rank[rank],
+            v_rank[rank],
+            local_sel,
+            local_table,
+            token_to_req,
+            False,
+            k_scale=k_scale,
+            v_scale=v_scale,
+            return_lse=True,

+        if rank:
+            assert torch.isneginf(lse[0]).all()
+        outs.append(out.float())
+        lses.append(lse.float())

+        torch.stack(outs),
+        torch.stack(lses),
+        return_lse=True,
+        is_lse_base_on_e=False,

+    )

The runner uses it, and `init_attn_backend` passes the same number to `create_metadata_builders` (new optional `block_table_width`), so the kernel block table is always runner width × (layer block / kernel block). **3. The layer's metadata builder sizes its kernel block table from the layer (selector) spec.** [`worker/utils.py#L325-L340`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c9de36da9b9551908a0ded2fd3185ae2ebfafc63/vllm/v1/worker/utils.py#L325-L340) (this code is from main, #57169):
```python
max_num_blocks = self.kv_cache_spec.max_num_blocks_per_req(...)              # selector spec, block 1920, replicated
width = get_block_table_width(max_num_blocks, self.kv_cache_spec.block_size)  # alignment by block 1920
width *= self.kv_cache_spec.block_size // kernel_block_size                  # * 1920 // 480 = 4
self.kernel_block_table = torch.zeros(..., width, ...)
```
- `max_num_blocks_per_req`: cdiv(262144, 1920) = **137**
- block_alignment = 128 / gcd(128, **1920**) = 1, so the width stays **137**
- × 4 → **548** kernel columns.

**4. The crash.** [`worker/utils.py#L404-L409`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c9de36da9b9551908a0ded2fd3185ae2ebfafc63/vllm/v1/worker/utils.py#L404-L409) receives a group row of 140 columns:
```python
out = self.kernel_block_table[ubatch_idx, :rows, : cols * blocks_per_kv_block]   # [:, :, :560] -> only 548 exist
torch.add(..., out=out.unflatten(1, (cols, -1)))                                # 548 is not 140 * k -> error
```

**Why main is safe and this branch is not:** the code in step 3 assumes every layer spec in a group has the group's block size. On main that holds. Step 1 adds a layer with a larger block (and a different DCP sharding) to the group, so the two width formulas (steps 2 and 3) round 137 to different multiples.

**When it fails, and when it does not fail but is wrong.** I ran the exact formulas of steps 2–3 and the exact ops of step 4 on CPU (torch 2.10) over 21,888 shapes (group block 16–1024, DCP 2/3/4/8, `max_model_len` 1,024–300,000):

| Result | Shapes | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Widths agree | 15,596 | correct |
| Widths differ, kernel width not a multiple of the row width | 6,115 | `unflatten` raises (our crash) |
| Widths differ, kernel width **is** a multiple of the row width | **177** | **no error**: `unflatten` succeeds with an inner size < DCP, and `torch.add(..., out=...)` only warns "An output with one or more elements was resized … deprecated" and resizes the output. The returned kernel block table has the wrong width; row 0 holds only the first part of its blocks, and rows ≥ 1 hold wrong block ids. |

The silent cases are mostly short `max_model_len` with large blocks, for example block 480, DCP 4, `max_model_len` 1024: the runner row is 4 columns, the kernel table is 4 wide but needs 16, and no error is raised. Reproducer:

```python
import math, torch
cdiv = lambda a, b: -(-a // b)
width = lambda n, blk: cdiv(n, 128 // math.gcd(128, blk)) * (128 // math.gcd(128, blk))  # get_block_table_width
b, d, L = 480, 4, 1024
n = cdiv(L, b * d)
cols, W = width(n, b), width(n, b * d) * d          # runner row (step 2), kernel table width (step 3)
table = torch.full((1, 3, W), -7, dtype=torch.int32)
bt = torch.arange(3 * cols, dtype=torch.int32).view(3, cols)
out = table[0, :3, : cols * d]                       # worker/utils.py:404
torch.add(torch.arange(d, dtype=torch.int32), bt.unsqueeze(-1), alpha=d,
          out=out.unflatten(1, (cols, -1)))          # worker/utils.py:405-410: warns, does not raise
expected = (bt.unsqueeze(-1) * d + torch.arange(d)).reshape(3, cols * d)
print(cols, W, out.shape, expected.shape)            # 4 4 torch.Size([3, 4]) torch.Size([3, 16])
print([torch.equal(out[r], expected[r, :W].int()) for r in range(3)])   # [True, False, False]
```

The existing tests use `max_model_len` = 784 × 16 with 2-column block tables, so they reach neither case.

### Proposed fix

Commit [`8e212b229`](https://github.com/kimseunghyun-kr/vllm/commit/8e212b229) on top of `c9de36da9` (branch `kimseunghyun-kr:qsa-dcp-59279-blockfix`).

**Idea:** compute the row width in one place, from the group spec, and give that same number to the builders.

1. New helper `get_kv_cache_group_block_table_width(group_spec, vllm_config, max_len)` in `vllm/v1/worker/block_table.py`. It is the runner's formula from step 2, moved into one function. The V2 runner now calls it.
2. `init_attn_backend` calls the same helper for each group and passes the result to `create_metadata_builders`:
   ```python
   block_table_width = get_kv_cache_group_block_table_width(
       kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups[kv_cache_group_id].kv_cache_spec,
       vllm_config,
       vllm_config.model_config.max_model_len,
   )
   group.create_metadata_builders(..., kernel_block_size=kernel_block_size,
                                  block_table_width=block_table_width)
   ```
3. `create_metadata_builders` uses that width when it is given, and keeps the old per-layer formula when it is not:
   ```diff
   -   max_num_blocks = self.kv_cache_spec.max_num_blocks_per_req(...)
   -   width = get_block_table_width(max_num_blocks, self.kv_cache_spec.block_size)
   +   if block_table_width is None:
   +       max_num_blocks = self.kv_cache_spec.max_num_blocks_per_req(...)
   +       block_table_width = get_block_table_width(max_num_blocks, self.kv_cache_spec.block_size)
   +   width = block_table_width
       width *= self.kv_cache_spec.block_size // kernel_block_size
   ```

So the kernel block table is always "runner row width × blocks per kernel block". In our case: 140 × 4 = 560 columns.

Tests added in `test_qsa_dcp_cache_policy.py` (CPU): the production shape (group 140 vs selector spec 137), and a full-width row mapped at DCP 4.

Not changed: the V1 runner path. Encoder-decoder models (the runner widens their rows past `max_model_len`) behave as before.
